description: Alternaria leaf spot is a fungal disease that mainly affects carrot leaves. It starts on older leaves and produces dark spots with yellow margins. In severe infections the leaves turn black, dry and die, causing major yield loss.
symptoms: Dark brown to black spots on leaves
Spots appear first on older leaves
Spots merge and form large dead areas
Leaves become black, dry and wither
Severe infection causes leaf blight and plant weakening
visual_signature: dark brown or black leaf spots
management: Treat seeds with hot water (50°C for 25–30 minutes)
Avoid dense planting to reduce humidity
Remove infected crop debris after harvest
Rotate crops for at least 3 years
similar_diseases: Cercospora leaf spot of carrot (Cercospora carotae)

differential_diagnosis.Alternaria_leaf_spot: dark brown to black lesions with yellow halos
differential_diagnosis.Cercospora_leaf_spot: light brown or tan circular lesions

impact: major yield losses during rainy seasons
source: CSIRO – Diseases of Vegetable Crops in Australia
Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development
